To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the blood serum lipid spectrum was significantly altered in patients with disturbed glucose tolerance, manifest type I and type II DM and that these changes were corrected in the course of therapy.
the lipid spectrum is altered in diabetes mellitus and this is a risk factor for the development of atherosclerosis and its complications.
in the course of diabetes mellitus the lipid metabolism undergoes significant changes, the severity of which depends on the type of DM, the stage of the disease and its therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the lipid spectrum in patients with disturbed glucose tolerance and manifest DM.
the lipid spectrum in diabetes, the lipid spectrum in diabetic patients and the lipid spectrum in patients with diabetes mellitus type 1 and type 2.

the study of the lipid spectrum in the blood serum of patients with disturbed GTTs and DM, the detection of lipid metabolism disturbances in the early stages of the disease, and the evaluation of the effectiveness of the treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lipid spectrum is a sensitive index of the metabolic state and the effectiveness of therapy in patients with DM.
the lipid spectrum in diabetes is altered and this alteration is a reflection of the metabolic derangement.
the lipid metabolism is significantly disturbed at the preclinical (disturbed GTT) stage of DM, and this is preserved at the clinical stage of DM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the blood serum lipid spectrum is a sensitive indicator of metabolic disturbances in diabetes mellitus and that the lipid spectrum can be used as an objective criterion in the diagnosis of the disease.
the lipid metabolism in patients of both types of DM is disturbed and the lipid spectrum changes in the time course and in accordance with the severity of the disease.

the blood serum lipid spectrum should be determined in persons with disturbed glucose tolerance, in order to detect the presence of lipid metabolic derangments at an early stage, to prevent the development of manifest forms of diabetes mellitus and to provide for the adequate treatment of this disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the blood serum lipid spectrum should be investigated at the preclinical and clinical stages of diabetes, since the lipid metabolic disturbances are a marker for early diagnostics and the effectiveness of therapy.
the blood lipid spectrum in diabetes patients is disturbed and the lipid spectrum is a sensitive marker for the diagnosis and monitoring of diabetes.
the lipid spectrum should be monitored in patients with DM, especially those with disturbed GTT.
